filename: Path-Conservative Well-Balanced High-Order Finite-Volume Solver for the Volume-Averaged Navier–Stokes Equations with Discontinuous Porosity.pdf
title: Path-conservative well-balanced high-order finite-volume solver for the volume-averaged Navier–Stokes equations with discontinuous porosity
testbed_rationale: The paper does not provide machine learning benchmarks or datasets; it introduces a numerical finite-volume solver and exact Riemann solver for 1D idealized volume-averaged Navier-Stokes equations.
pain_points: Discontinuous porosity generates non-conservative products where gradients cannot be defined in classical or distributional senses
Elliptic pressure Poisson solver in incompressible flow becomes challenging in the presence of discontinuities
Lack of standardized criteria for choosing physically admissible paths in path-conservative schemes across non-conservative jumps
extraction_notes: Supported by NSF STC LEAP (Award # 2019625-STC). This is a purely numerical/CFD methodology paper focusing on artificial compressibility, path-conservative WENO methods, and well-balanced schemes for volume-averaged Navier-Stokes equations with discontinuous porosity; no ML models or training are present.
